summary: Practise switchgear switching, inspection and maintenance planning with IEC-based scenarios. Review the course outline and see if it fits your role.
lede: High-voltage switchgear operation and maintenance covers controlled switching, inspection and upkeep of equipment that switches, protects and isolates high-voltage circuits. For electrical professionals working with high-voltage installations, the training develops practical methods for preparing switching sheets and isolation and earthing checklists, assessing inspection findings and test histories, interpreting relay event records, and prioritising maintenance and outage actions using IEC 62271 practices and IEC 60255 relay context.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits electrical professionals who already work with high-voltage installations and need consistent methods for switchgear operation, inspection and maintenance planning.
prerequisites: Prior work with electrical installations and familiarity with electrical safety procedures are expected. No coding or programming is required. Exercises use tabletop scenarios and sample switchgear records; they do not qualify you to perform live switching independently.
